Overview of the Automotive Industry  
18. The automotive industry is one of the key drive rs of the Indian economy. Since the 
liberalization of the sector in 1991 and allowing 1 00 per cent FDI through automatic route, Indian 
automobile sector has come a long way. In its writt en submission to the Committee, the Ministry 
informed that today, there is a presence of major g lobal auto manufacturers in the country. All 
categories of vehicles like two-wheelers, three wheelers, passenger cars, light commercial vehicles, 
trucks, buses, tractors, heavy commercial vehicles,  etc. are produced in India and that India is the 

8 
 
second largest manufacturer of 2-Wheelers, the larg est manufacturer of 3-Wheelers and the 3rd 
largest manufacturer of passenger cars in the world. The Ministry further stated that manufacturing 
of automobiles including trucks, buses, cars, three  wheelers/ two wheelers etc . in India has risen at 
a very high pace. The industry produced about 22.9 million vehicles including Passenger Vehicles, 
Commercial Vehicles, Three Wheelers, Two Wheelers a nd Quadricycles in financial year 2021-22 
and about 19.8 million vehicles have been produced during the months of April to December 2022. 
 
19. As regards the industry’s domestic automobile s ales for Passenger Vehicles, Commercial 
Vehicles, Three Wheelers, Two Wheelers and Quadricycles, the Ministry submitted that the sale in 
financial year 2021-22 was 17.5 million and 16 mill ion for April  to December 2022. The Ministry 
also apprised the Committee that the Indian auto co mponent industry, with a well evolved 
manufacturing ecosystem, produces a wide variety of  products including engine parts, drive 
transmission and steering parts, body and chassis, suspension and braking parts, equipment and 
electrical parts, besides others to service the dyn amic automobile industry. According to the 
National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), the auto industry provides direct employment to 
over 42 lakh people and indirect employment to 2.65  crore people. The automotive industry 
contributes 6% to India’s GDP and 35% to Manufacturing GDP. 
 
20. The Committee notes that the passenger car sect or of India grew significantly as India 
became the 3 
rd  largest manufacturer of passenger cars in the worl d.  At the same time, in 2-
Wheeler sector, India has slipped to 2 nd  position from the 1 st  position as compared to the 
FY2021-22. While the Committee commends the efforts  of the Ministry in respect of 
manufacture of passenger cars, it however notes wit h concern the decline in manufacturing 
of 2-Wheelers in view of the extensive use of 2-Whe elers in the country. The Committee is of 
the view that the Ministry should conduct a holisti c study and look into the shortcomings 
that have caused India to slip down to 2 nd  position in manufacturing of 2-Wheelers so that 
corrective measures can be taken timely to enable India to regain its position. 
 
Agricultural Machinery & Tractor Sector 
21.  Agricultural Machinery mainly consists of Agri cultural Tractors, Power Tillers, Combine 
Harvesters and other Agriculture Machineries & Impl ements. In its reply, the Ministry informed 
the Committee that due to negligible production of Power Tillers, Combine Harvesters and other 
Agricultural Machineries, this sector is mainly dom inated by Agricultural Tractors. Indian Tractor 
Industry is the largest in the world (excluding sub  20 HP belt driven tractors used in China), 
accounting for one third of the global production. The other tractor markets in the world are China 
and the United States. 
 
22. The Ministry also informed that Indian Tractors  were exported to US and other countries 
like Malaysia, Turkey, etc. Indian players have agg ressively started exporting to African countries 

9 
 
by bidding for government tender requirement. As su ch, Indian tractors are gaining acceptance in 
international markets. As the cost of tractors in I ndia is cheapest in the world, there is tremendous 
scope for improvement of export of tractors in future. 
 
23.  The Committee expresses its appreciation that Indian Tractor Industry has begun to 
make penetration slowly into the international mark et which is encouraging and laudable. 
However, it observes with concern that the producti on of Power Tillers, Combine Harvesters 
and other Agricultural Machineries are negligible a nd therefore recommends that the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries in coordination with t he Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare should work towards promotion of agricultur al tools and machinery which will 
ultimately boost the Agricultural Machinery Sector.  It is of the firm confidence that a robust 
push towards production of agricultural machineries  will go a long way in agriculture 
production of the country as well as bring in more revenue to the farmers. 
 
Electric Vehicles: Faster Adoption & Manufacturing of Electric (& Hybrid) Vehicles in India 
(FAME-India) Scheme 
 
24. Electric vehicles have been making headlines fo r decades. But it is only in recent years that 
EVs have been attracting seminal interest, innovation, and investments. Significantly, India has the 
world’s third-highest CO 2 emissions and the Government is advocating that em bracing EVs will 
help in reducing CO 2 and curbing air pollution. 
 
25. During the presentation on the Demands for Gran ts (2023-24) of the Ministry before the 
Committee, the Secretary of MHI stated that to redu ce dependency on fossil fuel and to address 
issues of vehicular emissions, the Government appro ved the scheme titled 'Faster Adoption and 
Manufacturing of Electric (&Hybrid) Vehicles in India' (FAME India) in March, 2015 for a period 
of 2 years w.e.f. 1
st  April, 2015. The Phase-I of FAME India Scheme has been extended from time 
to time till 31 March, 2019 with enhancement of tot al outlay to Rs. 895 crore. The Scheme had 
four focus areas i.e.  Technology Development, Demand Creation, Pilot Pro ject and Charging 
Infrastructure and it was successful in terms of cr eating the major policy discourse in Electric 
Mobility among all stakeholders including different  Departments of the Government of India and 
State Governments. 
26. The Secretary, MHI, further informed that, base d on the experience gained during Phase 1 
of FAME Scheme and suggestions of various stakehold ers, the Ministry notified Phase-II of the 
Scheme on the 8
th  March, 2019 for a period of 5 years, commencing fr om 1st April 2019, with an 
outlay of Rs. 10,000 crore. The main objective of t he scheme is to encourage faster adoption of 
Electric and Hybrid vehicles by way of offering upf ront incentive on purchase of Electric vehicles 
and also by establishing the necessary charging Inf rastructure required for electric vehicles. The 
scheme will help address the issues of environmenta l pollution and fuel security. In this phase of 

10 
 
the Scheme, more emphasis is given on electrificati on of public transportation that includes shared 
transport.

Safety of Electric Vehicles 
 54.  During the course of deliberations in the mee ting on the 20 
th  February, 2023, the 
Committee raised its concerns about incidents of fi re in the Electric Vehicles and suggested 

18 
 
installation of adequate safety measures in the Ele ctric Vehicles like fire extinguishing system in 
case of fire. The Ministry apprised the Committee t hat Ministry of Road, Transport and Highways 
looks after the safety aspect of the Electric Vehic les and that an expert committee has also been 
constituted and the committee has also given a repo rt. The Ministry informed the Committee that 
manufacturing guidelines for Electric Vehicles have  also been changed and after following these 
guidelines, there is less likelihood of such fire incidents taking place in the Electric Vehicles.  
 
55.  The Committee notes that the incidents of fire in E lectric Vehicles is a cause of concern 
and needs to be addressed properly. Most of the fir e catching incidents takes place in EVs when 
battery is damaged or punctured.  Apart from technical faults and manufacturing defec ts of 
batteries, many of the fire catching incidents may also be attributed to personal negligence of users 
by not taking proper precautions . The Committee recommends that the Ministry should  in 
consultation with the stakeholders analyse and asce rtain the root cause of fire incidents in 
EVs and find a solution for it so that such inciden ts do not take place so as to avoid any 
casualty. Besides, proper guidelines should be issu ed for the users and adequate awareness 
should be generated among the people regarding the proper usage of Electric Vehicles.  
 
56. The Committee recommends that adequate and inte rnationally accepted safety 
standards should be adopted to ensure safety of the  vehicles and its users. A proper venting 
mechanism for overheated cells in the battery must be put in place. Besides, the following 
safety measures to prevent fire hazards in the Electric Vehicles may be followed:  
(i) Use of fire-resistant materials such as aluminum, stainless steel, and other non-
combustible materials for the body of the electric vehicles.  
(ii) Use of fire-resistant insulation materials in the b attery compartment and other 
areas where the electric vehicle components are located.  
(iii) Installation of fire-extinguisher system in the bat tery compartment to 
extinguish any fires that may occur. 
(iv) Installation of fire-resistant wiring and other ele ctrical components to reduce 
the risk of fire due to short circuits.  
(v) Installation of fire-resistant brakes and other saf ety components to reduce the 
risk of fire due to friction.  
(vi) Installation of temperature sensors in the battery compartment to detect any 
overheating and activate the fire suppression system.  
(vii) Installation of battery management system to monito r the temperature and 
charge levels of the battery and alert the driver if any anomalies are detected.  
(viii) Installation of cooling system in the battery compa rtment to keep the 
temperature of the battery within a safe range.

modernization, technological upgradation or expansion. It contributes about 1.9 % to GDP.

strong bearing on the growth and employment generat ion in the user industries as it provides 
critical inputs, i.e.  machinery and equipment for the entire manufacturi ng sector and other related 
sectors.

the steps taken and plans conceived to revive and s trengthen the CPSEs within its 
administrative ambit in its Action Taken Replies. 
 
***** 
 
 
 

25 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE AT A GLANCE 
 
1. The Committee notes that the Budgetary allocation o f Rs 6171.63 crore for the 
Financial Year 2023-24 is the highest ever enhancem ent in comparison to the BE of the 
previous years. The Committee notes the significant enhanced fund allocation to the Ministry 
and hopes that the allocation would be utilized eff ectively in achieving the targets set by the 
Ministry for the Financial Year 2023-24. 
 (Para 7) 
 
2. The Committee also notes that the Ministry has been  able to utilize more than 99% of 
the funds provided at the RE Stage in the previous two Financial Years i.e.  2020-21 & 2021-
22. However, in the Financial Year 2022-23, the Min istry has been able to utilize only Rs. 
1428.71 crore, which is 44.36% of the RE allocation s of Rs. 3220.33 crore till 31.01.2023. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensur e that the entire fund allocated at the 
RE stage is utilized effectively in consonance with  the financial policy and henceforth should 
rationalize the expenditure throughout the year eve nly to avoid any uneven spending during 
the last quarter of the financial year in future. 
 (Para 8) 
 
3. The Committee observes that the expenditure of the Ministry under most of its minor 
heads was sluggish throughout the Financial Year 20 22-23, and even at the fag end of the 
financial year, expenditure under “ Revenue Section ” was barely 43.6% of the RE and most 
of the funds under “ Capital Section ” was surrendered at the RE stage, which reflects 
imprudent financial management and planning. The Co mmittee recommends that the 
Ministry should draw up a clear and comprehensible plan for the Financial Year 2023-24 so 
as to avoid accumulation of the unspent funds in th e last quarter of the financial year and 
refrain from spending more than 33% of the allocate d amount during the last quarter of the 
financial year contrary to the General Financial Rules.  
(Para 10) 
4. The Committee observes that for the Financial Year 2023-24, the Budget Projection of 
the Ministry was Rs 6574.93 crore against which Min istry of Finance has allocated Rs 
6171.63 crore, which is about 93.87% of the project ion, as such, there is a shortfall of Rs 
403.30 crore in allocation. The budgetary allocatio n for the major Schemes of Ministry such 
as FAME India and Scheme for Competitiveness in Cap ital Goods Sector have also shortfall 
in allocation for the FY2023-24. The Committee reco mmends that the Ministry should take 
all-out effort to strategize and utilize the major part of the allocations timely and if need be, 
allocation for more funds should be projected at th e RE stage to avoid any hindrance  in the 
effective implementation of these Flagship Schemes. 
 (Para 12) 

26 
 
5. The Committee notes that there were various unfores een circumstances such as 
Covid-19 Pandemic induced constraints, etc. due to which the major portions of the funds 
were surrendered in the FYs 2019-20, 2020-21 and 20 21-22. It was also observed that under 
the major and important Scheme for Enhancement of C ompetitiveness in Capital Goods 
Sector, surrender of huge amounts were made continu ously since FYs 2019-20 to 2021-22 
due to receipt of less number of proposals from the implementing agencies. The Committee is 
of the view that huge surrender of funds defeats the very objective of the schemes envisioned. 
The Committee desires that the Ministry should anal yze and find out the reasons why 
adequate number of proposals were not received unde r the scheme and should devise a plan 
to promote the Schemes through awareness programmes /campaigns so that the funds made 
available to the Schemes are properly utilized and the goal of Make in India  and Atmanirbhar 
Bharat  Mission  is realized for the overall economic development of the country. 
 (Para 17) 
 
6. The Committee notes that the passenger car sector of India grew significantly as India 
became the 3 rd  largest manufacturer of passenger cars in the worl d.  At the same time, in 2-
Wheeler sector, India has slipped to 2 nd  position from the 1 st  position as compared to the 
FY2021-22. While the Committee commends the efforts  of the Ministry in respect of 
manufacture of passenger cars, it however notes wit h concern the decline in manufacturing 
of 2-Wheelers in view of the extensive use of 2-Whe elers in the country. The Committee is of 
the view that the Ministry should conduct a holisti c study and look into the shortcomings 
that have caused India to slip down to 2 nd  position in manufacturing of 2-Wheelers so that 
corrective measures can be taken timely to enable India to regain its position.  
(Para 20) 
 
7. The Committee expresses its appreciation that India n Tractor Industry has begun to 
make penetration slowly into the international mark et which is encouraging and laudable. 
However, it observes with concern that the producti on of Power Tillers, Combine Harvesters 
and other Agricultural Machineries are negligible a nd therefore recommends that the 
Ministry of Heavy Industries in coordination with t he Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers 
Welfare should work towards promotion of agricultur al tools and machinery which will 
ultimately boost the Agricultural Machinery Sector.  It is of the firm confidence that a robust 
push towards production of agricultural machineries  will go a long way in agriculture 
production of the country as well as bring in more revenue to the farmers. 
 (Para 23) 
 
 
 

27 
 
8. The Committee notes that 100% of the budget allocat ed at the RE stage under Phase-
II of the FAME Scheme has been utilized by the Mini stry in the Financial Years 2019-20 to 
2021-22 which reflects the sincerity, commitment an d determination with which the Scheme 
has been implemented and the funds utilized for pop ularizing the Electric Mobility in the 
country. The Committee, while expressing its concer n regarding the fuel security amidst 
global uncertainties as well as vehicular emissions , welcomes the efforts being made through 
the FAME-Scheme for transition to electric mobility . However, the expenditure as against 
the budget allotted at the RE stage i.e.  Rs. 2897.84 crore for the FY 2022-23 has not reach ed 
even halfway-mark till 08.02.2023 with less than tw o months left in the current financial 
year. The Committee recommends that the Ministry sh ould speed up the process and make 
earnest efforts to ensure optimal utilization of th e unspent funds in consonance with the 
Financial Rules during the Financial Year 2022-23.   
 (Para 29) 
 
9. The Phase-II of the FAME Scheme which has set the t arget to support 15,62,090 
vehicles within the timeline of 5 years is about to  complete 4 years and till 31.12.2022 has 
achieved only 51.96% of the target by supporting 8, 11,725 vehicles. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should put greater emp hasis on the implementation of the 
Scheme and prepare a blueprint to increase the sales of Electric Vehicles in consultation with 
the stakeholders and ensure that the targets are ac hieved. Besides, the Committee 
recommends that, in order to meet the set targets o f the scheme, the possibility of extending 
subsidies and incentives to the private vehicles sh ould be explored along with considering the 
incentives such as exemption from road tax, registr ation fee etc. on the purchase of electric 
vehicles which would help accelerate the acceptance of Electric Mobility in the country. 
 (Para 31) 
 
10. The Committee notes that the Ministry has under-per formed in respect of supporting 
e-3W and e-4W and in case of e-buses only a few cit ies are covered under the Scheme. India 
is a vast country and providing e-buses only to a f ew big cities will not able to resolve the 
issues of the rising fossil fuel imports and vehicu lar air pollution adequately. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should expand the scop e of the scheme for other smaller cities 
and, if required, seek enhancement in the budget al location at the RE stage from the 
Ministry of Finance so as to reach its optimum pote ntial to increase uptake of the electric 
buses to promote green energy.  
 (Para 34) 
 
 
 

28 
 
11. The Committee is of the view that charging infrastr ucture is critical for successfully 
switching over to the EV mode of transport and expr esses its concern that EV charging 
stations have been sanctioned only for a few cities , expressways and highways. For the 
effective promotion of the EVs throughout the count ry, it is needless to say that more 
charging stations need to be installed. The Committ ee recommends that the Ministry should 
approach the Ministry of Finance for enhanced alloc ation of funds at the RE stage, so that 
the requirements of installing more charging facilities under the FAME-II Scheme are met to 
give a much needed boost to the Electric Mobility.  
(Para 36) 
 
12. The Committee notes the higher allocation of Rs 517 1.97 crore made under the 
FAME-II Scheme for the Financial Year 2023-24, whic h constitutes more than 80% of the 
total budget of the Ministry, which would provide g reater thrust to the electric mobility in 
the country. The Committee also notes that the majo r portion of the fund allocated under 
FAME-II Scheme for the FY2023-24 is for the Buses a nd Chargers, i.e. Rs 3179 crores with 
around Rs. 180 crore for the chargers and rest for the buses. However, the Ministry has not 
been able to install most of the Chargers under the  FAME Scheme and therefore, the 
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas has been rope d in on the proposal to roll out 
charging stations in the retail outlets of Public S ector Units. The Committee appreciates the 
decision of the Ministry as Public Sector Units in oil industries are more apt and already in 
the business of providing energy solutions to the c ountry and such tie up will result in faster 
realization of the Scheme. 
 (Para 38) 
 
13. The Committee notes that FAME-II Scheme was notifie d for 5 years and has a 
deadline of 31 st  March 2024 to complete its targets of supporting 1 5.62 lakh electric vehicles. 
Indian automotive industry is of the size of about Rs.10, 00,000 crores and in the FY 2021-22, 
there was a total production of 2.29 crore vehicles  in the country, out of which there were 
1.75 crores domestic sales. In a country like India , supporting only 15.62 lakh electric 
vehicles may not be enough to reduce the carbon emi ssions & improve the air quality and to 
save forex on fossil fuel imports. The Committee is  of the opinion that the Phase-II of the 
FAME Scheme should be extended further with new tar gets, incentives and measures to give 
boost to the electric mobility in the country. Furt hermore, as one of the objectives of 
transition to electric mobility is to improve the a ir quality, the Committee is of the view that 
the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Cha nge may be roped in as partner player 
in the implementation of FAME-II Scheme.  
(Para 39) 
 

29 
 
14. As the Vehicle Scrapping Policy of the Ministry of Road, Transport & Highways, 
provides various incentive mechanisms to induce End -of-life vehicle owners to scrap older 
vehicles like good scrap value for old vehicles, re gistration fee waiver on purchase of new 
vehicles, tax concessions by State Governments, upf ront discount by auto Original 
Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) etc., the Committee recommends that the Ministry 
should collaborate with other concerned Ministries for a holistic promotion of EVs and also 
work out a comprehensive policy to give incentives on purchase of new Electric Vehicles to 
the End-of-life vehicle owners, which will go a long way in encouraging the faster adoption of 
the Electric Vehicles and promoting environment friendly transportation in the country.  
(Para 41) 
 
15. The Committee was informed that the Production Link ed Incentive (PLI) Scheme for 
Automobile and Auto Components is expected to attra ct investment of around Rs 67,690 
crore and will generate around 1.45 lakh direct emp loyment. Eighty five (85) applicants, 
both overseas and Indian, have been approved under the components of this scheme. As per 
the data provided by MHI, the actual expenditure un der this scheme for the FY 2022-23 till 
31 st  January, 2023 is nil and the RE amount of Rs. 10.74 crore is lying unutilized which is not 
a good reflection of expenditure management in view  of the importance of the Scheme to 
promote domestic manufacturing as a part of Make in India  and Atmanirbhar Bharat  
Mission . The Committee is of the view that a yearly action  plan with time-frame should be 
devised for optimum utilization of funds under the Scheme and its effective implementation.  
(Para 45) 
 
16. As per the data provided by the Ministry, the RE fo r the FY 2022-23 is fully utilized. 
However, the budget allocated for this Scheme is Rs 1.00 crore for the financial year 2023-24. 
The Committee is of the view that this is an ambiti ous scheme which will facilitate in 
realizing the goal of Make in India  and Atmanirbhar Bharat  by promoting newer and niche 
technologies and therefore needs to be implemented timely and effectively. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should complete its pr e-requisites in the gestation period by 
providing necessary support for setting up and comm issioning of manufacturing facilities by 
the beneficiary firms and if required, seek for enhanced allocation at the RE stage so that the 
scheme is implemented effectively and proved to be efficacious.  
(Para 50) 
 
17. Taking note of the  report of the economic think ta nk, Global Trade Research 
Initiative (GTRI) as reported by the Indian Express  dated the 8 th  March, 2023, the 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should look into the issues raised therein 
holistically with a view to address the concerns an d apprehensions with regard to the 

30 
 
viability of the electric mode of transport and the  dependence on China for battery 
production and apprise the Committee in this regard.  
 (Para 53) 
 
18. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should i n consultation with the 
stakeholders analyse and ascertain the root cause o f fire incidents in EVs and find a solution 
for it so that such incidents do not take place so as to avoid any casualty. Besides, proper 
guidelines should be issued for the users and adequate awareness should be generated among 
the people regarding the proper usage of Electric Vehicles.  
 (Para 55) 
 
19. The Committee recommends that adequate and internat ionally accepted safety 
standards should be adopted to ensure safety of the  vehicles and its users. A proper venting 
mechanism for overheated cells in the battery must be put in place. Besides, the following 
safety measures to prevent fire hazards in the Electric Vehicles may be followed:  
(i) Use of fire-resistant materials such as aluminum, stainless steel, and other non-
combustible materials for the body of the electric vehicles.  
(ii) Use of fire-resistant insulation materials in the b attery compartment and other 
areas where the electric vehicle components are located.  
(iii) Installation of fire-extinguisher system in the bat tery compartment to 
extinguish any fires that may occur. 
(iv) Installation of fire-resistant wiring and other ele ctrical components to reduce 
the risk of fire due to short circuits.  
(v) Installation of fire-resistant brakes and other saf ety components to reduce the 
risk of fire due to friction.  
(vi) Installation of temperature sensors in the battery compartment to detect any 
overheating and activate the fire suppression system.  
(vii) Installation of battery management system to monito r the temperature and 
charge levels of the battery and alert the driver if any anomalies are detected.  
(viii) Installation of cooling system in the battery compa rtment to keep the 
temperature of the battery within a safe range. 
 (Para 56) 
 
20. The Committee is of the view that enhancement of Co mpetitiveness in Capital Goods 
Sector is vital for its successful expansion, which  plays an important role in boosting the 
growth in manufacturing sector and accelerating the  growth trajectory of the country. As 
constraints faced due to shortage of funds are undesirable for the effective implementation of 
the Scheme, the Committee recommends that the Minis try should timely utilize the funds 
and make effort to compensate the shortfall at the RE Stage. The Committee also notes that 

31 
 
no allocation has been made for industry associations and PSUs for undertaking promotional 
activities for the development of capital goods sec tor. The Committee is of the view that 
promotional activities for development of capital g oods sector are important to disseminate 
the benefits of schemes of the Government to the st akeholders and the Ministry should take 
up the matter with the Ministry of Finance for a re -look on budgetary projection for 
undertaking promotional activities by industry associations and PSUs.  
(Para 63) 
 
21. The Committee notes that, under autonomous bodies, only Central Manufacturing 
Technology Institute (CMTI) has been sanctioned fun ds under the BE for the FY 2023-24, 
and there has been no provision of funds for other autonomous bodies. In the present time, 
R&D and technological upgradation are of critical i mportance to keep pace with the global 
competition. The Committee recommends that the Mini stry should also focus on other R&D 
institutions as well and provide them the necessary  budgetary support for the advancement 
of technology. The budget allotted to CMTI, Bengalu ru should be utilized optimally to get 
the desired results and if the need arises, the Min istry may seek for enhancement of 
allocation at the RE stage. 
 (Para 65) 
 
22. The Committee notes with dismay that year after yea r the number of Central Public 
Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) under the control of the  Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) are 
decreasing. The Committee recommends that the Minis try should work towards enhancing 
the performance of CPSEs under its control and adop t restructuring measures to revive the 
loss making CPSEs so that no further closure of the  CPSEs takes place. In view of the fact 
that while privately run enterprises/industries are  thriving ever in the competitive market 
conditions, the Ministry should take a serious and holistic analysis of the causes making its 
PSEs sick and loss-making and make concerted effort s for their revival/restoration. The 
steps taken in this regard may be furnished to the Committee at the time of Action Taken 
Replies .  
(Para 69) 
 
23. The Committee observes that the actual utilisation of funds till 31.01.2023 in case of a 
number of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)  through Internal & Extra Budgetary 
Resources (IEBR) as against the RE 2022-23 is very negligible.  The Committee recommends 
that the Ministry should find out the reasons for t he under-utilisation of IEBR and ensure 
that the funds raised are properly utilised before the end of financial year.  
(Para 71) 
 

32 
 
24. Out of the 16 Operational CPSEs under the administr ative control of the Ministry of 
Heavy Industries, 5 CPSEs namely Engineering Projec ts (India) Limited (EPIL), Heavy 
Engineering Corporation (HEC), Hindustan Machine To ols (HMT), Rajasthan Electronics 
and Instruments Limited (REIL) and NEPA Ltd. are lo ss making CPSEs. It has been 
observed that HEC is a loss making enterprise conti nuously for the past several years. 
Despite the loss-making status of HEC, a meagre tok en amount of Rs 0.01 crore has been 
kept as a budgetary support for the enterprise in B E for the Financial Year 2023-24. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry should make concerted efforts to improve the 
situation of HEC and if need arises, may seek addit ional funds at RE stage and also furnish 
the steps taken and plans conceived to revive and s trengthen the CPSEs within its 
administrative ambit in its Action Taken Replies.  
(Para 74)

INTRODUCTION 
  
  
 I, the Chairman of the Department -related Parliamentary Standing Committee on 
Industry, having been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this T hree Hundred 
and Twenty Second Report on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Micro, Small and 
Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s T hree

Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee welcomes the goal of the Government for making 
India a $5 trillion economy by the Year 2024 -25 and opines that the target  
can be achieved by growth and development of the MSME sector. As MSME 
sector is vital for fostering entrepreneurship and generating self -
employment opportunities at comparatively lower capital cost and are 
complementary to large industries as ancillary units, formulation of targeted 
policies in the areas of infrastructure development, technological 
upgradation and forward linkages could help MSMEs to achieve their full 
potential and propel the Indian economy to a higher growth trajectory. The 
Committee rec ommends that Government need to play a proactive role in 
promoting MSME Sector by handholding the MSMEs at the grassroots level 
and for this, a top down approach needs to be implemented right down to 
the last tier of the MSME sector in letter, spirit and a ction. In this regard, a 
roadmap should be devised to achieve the desired results.  
(Para 10) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
The Government implements various schemes, programmes and 
initiatives for the promotion, development and enhancing the competiveness 
of MSME  sector in the country. A number of recent initiatives have been 
taken to strengthen, support, finance, revive and reconstruct MSMEs. These 
include:  
(i) Rs. 50,000 crore equity infusion through Self Reliant India Fund. This 
scheme has a provision of Rs.10 , 000 crore from Government of India and 
Rs.40,000 Crore leverage through Private Equity/Venture Capital funds. 
This initiative is aimed at providing growth capital to the deserving and 
eligible units of MSME sector.  
(ii) New revised criteria for classification of MSMEs. 
(iii) No global tenders for procurement up to Rs. 200 crore. 
(iv) “Udyam Registration” for MSMEs, for Ease of Doing Business w.e.f. 
1.7.2020 

 4 
(v) Launching of an online Portal “Champions” in June, 2020 to cover 
many aspects of e -governance including grievance redress and handholding 
of MSMEs. 
(vi) Inclusion of Retail and Wholesale traders as MSMEs w.e.f. 2.7. 2021. 
(vii) Non-tax benefits extended for 3 years in case of an upward change in 
status of MSMEs. 
(viii) Launch of Udyam Assist Platfo rm on 11.1.2023 to bring Informal 
Micro Enterprises (IMEs) under the formal ambit for availing the benefits 
under Priority Sector Lending.  
(ix) The Ministry of MSME , vide notification no. S.O. 5670(E) dated 
9.11.2018, had made it mandatory for all Centra l Government  Ministries/ 
Departments/ CPSUs to procure at least 25% of their annual procurement 
from MSEs, including 3% from MSEs owned by women entrepreneurs. 
(x) Field offices of Ministry of MSME organize various awareness 
campaigns for UDYAM registrati on and benefits of Government schemes 
/programmes, in coordination with MSME/ Industry Departments of 
States/UTs concerned and other MSME stakeholders through physical 
workshops, social media, print media & electronic media for creating wide 
publicity for increasing participation from all stake holders.  
(xi) In order to address the issue of delayed payment to MSMEs, RBI has 
issued guidelines for setting up and operating the Trade Receivables 
Discounting System (TReDS) to facilitate the financing of trade r eceivables 
of MSMEs from corporate and other buyers, including government 
departments and public sector undertakings (PSUs) through multiple 
financiers electronically.  
(xii).  Budget 2023-24, has announced the infusion of Rs. 9,000 crore in the 
corpus of CGTMSE to enable additional credit of Rs. 2.00 lakh crore with a 
reduced cost of credit.

opportunities in urban and rural areas; providing adequate employment to 

 8

The following steps have been taken to reduce t he rate of rejections by 
banks in order to further improve the efficiency of the scheme: 
i. Ministry of MSME has simplified the existing PMEGP guideline by 
discontinuing the role of District Level Task Force Committee 
(DLTFC) for recommendation of proposal/ap plications to financing 
banks.  
ii. Further, the Implementing agencies evaluate the applications based on 
Score Card devised by Indian Banks' Association (IBA) and forward 
to financing banks for taking credit decision based on techno -
economic viability of the project. 
iii. Technical and financial experts have been engaged to provide 
handholding support to the PMEGP beneficiaries. 
iv. Model Detailed Project Reports on various industries have been 
uploaded on the PMEGP portal for prospective beneficiaries 

 12 
v. Industrial solutions are presented through webinars for setting up of 
micro enterprises every Sunday for the awareness of youth and 
prospective entrepreneurs. 
vi. Meetings with bank officials are conducted at Zonal and HQ level to 
impress upon the banks for removal of trivial  reasons of rejections 
like „PMEGP target achieved‟ and „Out of service area‟. 
Through these efforts, the rejection rate for PMEGP applications 
forwarded to banks has reduced from 58% to 43% during 2021 -22 to 2022-
23. Further efforts are being made in co -ordination with all stake holders to 
reduce the rejection rate by improving application quality and by minimizing 
rejection on avoidable grounds.

9. The Committee notes that the BE for SFURTI Scheme for the FY 
2022-23 was Rs. 33 4.00  crore which was reduced drastically to Rs. 1.95 
crore only at the RE Stage due to the introduction of a new system of 
accounting according to which the amount was reduced to Rs. 1.95 crore 
and the Ministry concentrated in utilizing the unspent balanc e of Rs. 200.00 
crore lying with different implementing and nodal agencies.  In this regard, 
the Committee was apprised that in the old system, the money used to be 
kept in banks and so the amount remained unutilized whereas in the new 
system the money com es to the Central Nodal Agency (CNA) where the 
unspent balance is first collected and then depending upon the actual 
expenditure in the field, the money is released, thereby helping in 
disbursement of money. The Committee is of the view that the new system  of 
accounting should be accessible to the beneficiary actually in need and a 
clear set of guidelines from the top to the bottom should be put in place for 
accessibility of the intended beneficiary. The Committee appreciates the BE 
of Rs. 280.00 crore for the SFURTI Scheme for the FY 2023 -2024 and 
recommends that the allocation should be utilized optimally for employment 
generation and benefit of the artisans.  
(Para 51) 
Action Taken Replies  
Under the new fund flow mechanism introduced by Dep artment of 
Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, the account of the Central Nodal Agency 
(CNA) has been mapped with the accounts of the Sub Agencies (SA) i.e, 
the Nodal Agencies (NA) for effective implementation of SFURTI projects. 

 13 
Besides, all the accounts of the Implement ing Agencies (IA)/Special 
Purpose Vehicle (SPV) are also being mapped with the Sub Agency 
accounts to extend desired benefits of the scheme to the beneficiaries. Also, 
the scheme is under review for continuation beyond 30.9.2022. 136 clusters 
are proposed to be set up during the FY 2023 -24. Under the revised fund 
flow mechanism, the BE of Rs 280.00 crore for the FY 2023 -24 will be 
utilized towards development of the 136 clusters directly benefitting 81600 
artisans as well as in meeting the requirements of already approved clusters.

10. The Committee observes that coir being a traditional product, there is 
enough scope for skill development. Therefore, training and up -skilling 
become imperative for the growth and proliferation of  coir industry into the 
untested, non -traditional areas of coir products. The  Committee 
recommends that training programmes, including training and skill 
development in areas of technological innovations, should be organized for 
the artisans at field level  at regular intervals to enhance their skill and 
output for overall development of the coir sector. 
(Para 59) 
Action Taken Replies   
The Coir Industry is a labour intensive and export oriented industry 
employing more than seven lakh of workers predominantl y women.  Skill 
development is the most essential pre -requisite for the overall development 
of the industry and to accelerate the spread of the industry into non -
traditional areas. Development of skilled manpower in coir industry through 
appropriate traini ng programmes is one of the major activities of Coir 
Board.   
Considering the importance of skill development, in order to create a 
skilled manpower in the Coir Industry in all coir producing states of the 
Country, Coir Board is implementing various skill development 
programmes under the Umbrella Scheme - Coir Vikas Yojana under the 
component „Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana‟ in all coir 
producing states of the country through its various field offices, which will 
uplift the soft skills of artisans  and thereby encouraging them to start their 
own industry/units. Under this Scheme, the following skill training 
programmes are being implemented by the Board through its various field 
offices located all over the country: 

 14 
•Training in manufacturing of Val ue Added Products (VAP) – Duration 2 
months with a Stipend Rs.3000/ - per month (increased from Rs.3000 to 
Rs.6000 with effect from 2021-22). 
•Training in Spinning under Mahila Coir Yojana (MCY) - Duration 2 
months with a Stipend Rs.3000/ - per month (increa sed from Rs.3000 to 
Rs.6000 with effect from 2021-22). 
•Diploma Course in Coir Technology (NSQF Level -4) –Duration 1 year, 
Internship- 3 months, Stipend Rs.3000/- per month (increased from Rs.3000 
to Rs.6000 with effect from 2021-22). 
•Certificate Course o f Coir Artisan in Coir Technology (NSQF Level -3) 
Duration 6 months, Internship - 1 month, Stipend Rs.3000/ - per month 
(increased from Rs.3000 to Rs.6000 with effect from 2021-22). 
Out of the above training programmes, the regular training 
programmes of the Board viz. NSQF Level 3 & 4 are imparted through 
Board‟s Offices, viz. NCT&DC, Kalavoor, REC, Thanjavur, Regional 
Office, Bhubaneswar and Regional Office, Rajahmundry only.   
Coir Board, through the above training programmes, has been 
imparting theory clas ses and practical training in areas of fibre extraction, 
spinning of coir yarn, weaving, manufacture of mats, mattings, handicraft 
items etc.  The trainees get the opportunity to learn the diversified 
applications of coir and it‟s by products, technological  innovations on coir 
etc. Further, Orientation Training Programmes and Trainer‟s Training 
Programmes is conducted on need basis. 
Recommendation/Observation 
11. The Committee appreciates the export performance of coir and coir 
products during the years 2020-21 and 2021-22 as the targets were achieved 
by the Coir Board. Further, the Committee notes that Coir pith with export 
earnings of Rs 1,349.63 crore constitutes 49 per cent of the total export of 
coir products and Coir fibre with export earnings of Rs  498.43 crore 
constitutes 18 per cent of the total exports. Afte r 2014 -15, the value 
generated from the export of non -traditional coir and coir products 
overtakes the value generated from the export of traditional coir and coir 

 15 
products. Export Market Promotion Scheme helps exporters in reaching out 
to overseas market and helps in getting much -needed business deals to 
support the industry. Thus, the role of the Coir Board is increasing as a 
promoter and facilitator of the industry and its focus should be on 
facilitating market-oriented development of the coir sector. The Committee 
is of the view that Coir Board should explore reaching out to overseas 
markets which are still out of the ambit of export destination. Possibility of 
displaying coir products at the In dian Missions abroad should also be 
explored in order to create demand for coir products in overseas markets. 
Coir Board should also support in establishing fibre/yarn bank for sourcing 
quality raw material to facilitate making quality traditional as well as non-
traditional coir products for expanding export markets.  
 
(Para 61) 
Action Taken Replies 
  
Export Promotion is one of the thrust areas  in the  promotional 
agenda of Coir Board aimed towards sustainable development of the Indian 
coir industry. The maj or export promotional tools implemented by Coir 
Board in association with trade and industry are participation in international 
fairs in India and abroad on a focus - country/focus-product basis, 
international seminars and conferences, organizing workshops/ Management 
Development Programmes, extending financial assistance to entrepreneurs 
under the International Co -operation Scheme for various export promotion 
activities, encouraging exports and export related activities by presentation 
of  Coir Industry aw ards etc.  All the international events are undertaken as 
per the guidelines of International Cooperation Scheme of the Ministry of 
MSME.   Besides, the display of coir products through Indian Council for 
Cultural Relations in Indian Missions abroad is und erway for making 
awareness about coir and coir products among the people in the respective 
countries.  The possibility for establishing coir fibre/yarn bank is being 
explored for sourcing quality raw material to produce quality coir products 
necessary for expanding export markets, in coordination with respective 
State Governments.

21. The Committee notes that introduction of Guaranteed Emergency 
Credit Line (GECL) Scheme was a welcome move by the Government to 
provide much -needed financial assistance to MSMEs affected by the 
COVID-19 Pandemic. However, the utilization of the allocated amount of 
Rs. 15000.00 crore for the FY2022 -23, which was reduced to Rs. 10,500.00 
crore at the RE Stage, is not very encouraging as the actual exp enditure (as 
on 31.01.2023) is Rs. 7500.00 crore only (i.e. 72 per cent of the RE 
allocation). The Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that 
the allocated amount of Rs. 14,100.00 crore for the FY2023 -24 is optimally

have suffered due to the Covid -19 Pandemic are benefitted and the off take 
of loan is enhanced for their overall growth and development.   
 (Para 128) 
Action Taken Replies 
Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) was announced 
as part of the Aatma Nirbhar Bharat Package in 2020 with the objective to 
help MSMEs/small businesses to meet their operational liabilities and 
resume businesses in view of the distress caused by the COVID-19 crisis, by 
providing Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) 100 per cent guarantee in 
respect of the credit facility extended by them to eligible borrowers.  
ECLGS is not a beneficiary -oriented scheme; rather it is a guarantee 
scheme which provides guarantee to MLIs to encourag e them to lend to 
eligible borrowers under the scheme. The amount disbursed under the 
scheme to National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC), 
the agency operating the scheme, is to be utilized to meet the claims arising 
out of defaults under t he scheme, if any. Since the launch of ECLGS, actual 
defaults under the scheme has been less than that estimated at the time of 
introduction of the scheme and hence the utilisation of funds for meeting the 
claims arising out of the guarantee issued has bee n on the lower side. 
Lending to borrowers under ECLGS by MLIs by availing guarantees from 

 24 
NCGTC has no correlation to utilisation of funds. Loans have continued to 
be extended to eligible borrowers under the Scheme by the MLIs and 
guarantees were issued by  NCGTC upon application made by MLIs. Thus, 
borrowers have not been adversely impacted due to the lower utilisation of 
funds.  
  With respect to the Budget under the GECL, an amount of Rs. 15,000 
crore was allocated at the BE Stage, as per the request of t he implementing 
agency and for efficient & optimally utilized of the funds, it was reduced to 
Rs. 10,500 crore at RE stage.  Funds allocated at RE stage have been 100% 
utilized.

 The Committee notes the increase in  the procurement from

study visit to Udaipur, Mumbai and Goa in April, 2023, the Committee 
observed that many of the Public Sector Undertakings are unable to 
fulfill the mandatory procurement of 4 per cent from the SC/ST MSEs 
either due to their non -participation or due to their non -availability. 
Therefore, greater pus h in that direction is the need. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry should coordinate with the PSUs and 
take steps with set targets, including Vendor Development Programmes, 
so that the PSUs are able to meet the sub-target procurement of 4 per 
cent from MSEs as mandated under the Public Procurement Policy. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
45. The Committee is of the view that the procedure of availing the credit 
facility should be simplified by reducing the paperwork, including 
streamlining the applicat ion process and introducing online loan 
applications, and documentation requirements for loan applications should 
be in regional languages so that MSMEs even in rural areas can easily avail 
the credit facility.  
(Para 100) 
Action Taken Replies 
 
In regard t o the procedure of availing the credit facility it is to 
mention that to avail the credit online portal such as  
www.psbloansin59minutes.com & www.udyamimitra.in are a vailable 
through which an applicant may apply for availing the credit facilities. 
Moreover, in association with State Governments CGTMSE is providing 
additional guarantee coverage to MSE‟s loans.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee apprecia tes the efforts of the Ministry to make 
available the online credit portals viz. www.psbloansin59minutes.com & 
www.udyamimitra.in through which an applicant may apply for 

 48 
availing the credit facilities. The Committee recommends that the loan 
formalities, including documentation requirements, should also be made 
available in regional languages  and processing of the loan applications 
should be monitored by a dedicated tea m of officers for timely disposal 
of loan applications. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
46. The Committee notes that an allocation of Rs. 24.96 crore was made 
for the Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme for MSMEs for 
the FY2022-23 which was enhanced  to Rs. 40 crore at the RE stage but the 
actual expenditure as on 31.01.2023 was only Rs. 9.52 crore, i.e. 25 per cent 
of the RE allocation.  On the other hand, the projected BE for the FY2023 -
24 is Rs. 96.35 crore, which is significantly higher than any p revious BE 
and RE allocation. While the Committee appreciates  the higher BE for the 
FY2023-24 for the PMS Scheme which would help significantly in 
development of MSME Sector of the country, the Committee recommends 
that optimal and full utilization of the  allocation should be ensured in order 
to make the Scheme efficacious. 
(Para 124) 
Action Taken Replies 
         Expenditure under the Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) 
Scheme as on 31.01.2023 was Rs 9.52 crore against RE of Rs 40 crore. 
However, the actual expenditure under the scheme- increased in the next two 
months and reached to Rs 27.52 crores (as on 31.03.2023) against revision in 
RE from Rs 40 crore to Rs 28.68 crore, thereby making it 95.95 % of the RE 
allocation. Optimal and full utilization of Rs. 96.35 crore allocated in BE for 
FY 2023-24 shall be ensured. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
The Committee is of the view that Procurement and Marketing 
Support (PMS) Scheme is the main stay of MSME Sect or and requires 
stringent supervision and complete utilisation of funds. The Budgetary 
support extended in FY 2023 -24 is quite magnanimous. In view of the 
fact that it is more than 3 times the amount actually utilised in FY 2022-
23, the Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure proper 
monitoring of this scheme to ensure complete utilisation of allocated 
funds in FY2023-24. 

 49 
Recommendation/Observation 
47. Fund of Funds, also called the Self Reliant India (SRI) Fund, has been 
formulated for addressing the equity funding challenges of MSME s ector 
and give them a thrust to break their barriers, encourage corporatization 
and allow them to grow to their full potential to become global champions. 
It was observed by the Committee that the Actual Expenditure of Rs. 212.57 
crore (up to 31.01.2023) h as been utilized which is only 53.66 per cent of 
the RE allocation of Rs. 439.40 crore for the FY 2022 -23. The Committee 
recommends that the remaining amount should be utilized in consonance 
with the Financial Rules and the BE allocation of Rs. 575.00 cror e for the 
FY 2023-24 should be utilized optimally and evenly throughout the year. 
(Para 133) 
Action Taken Replies 
         During the current Financial year 2022 -23, the RE was revised to 
392.79 crore and entire amount has been utilized.  
The Ministry of MSME will ensure that the amount would be utilized 
in consonance with the Financial Rules and the BE allocation of Rs. 575.00 
crore for the FY 2023-24 should be utilized optimally and evenly throughout 
the year. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Comm ittee notes that a substantial increase in Budgetary 
Support has been extended to the Fund of Funds, also called the Self 
Reliant India (SRI) Fund . Keeping in view the importance of equity 
funding challenges of MSME Sector, the Committee recommends that 
regular monitoring of fund utilization should be ensured in order to 
enable 100 per cent utilization in FY 2023-24. 
 

 50 
CHAPTER – IV 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH 
THE 
FINAL REPLIES OF THE MINISTRY ARE STILL AWAITED 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
48. The Committee is of the view that the  new classification of MSMEs 
would bring about positive changes in the MSME Sector including many 
benefits that will aid MSMEs to grow in size by attracting investments and 
would generate more employment opportuni ties. In this regard, in the 
deposition by the Secretary, Ministry of MSME on 20.02.2023 before the 
Committee, it emerged that although the change in definition of MSMEs is 
for their benefit, however, a study is required for sector -wise segregation of 
the MSMEs. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should carry out 
a study for sector -wise segregation of the MSMEs in order to ensure 
targeted distribution of budgetary allocations which would facilitate 
development, expansion and growth of the MSME sector. 
(Para 8) 
Action Taken Replies 
The Udyam Registration Portal of this Ministry captures data of 
activities based on NIC codes of registered MSMEs, including sector -wise 
data of MSMEs. As recommended by Committee, the sector -wise analysis 
of MSME data will be undertaken by the M/o MSME.   
 
Recommendation/Observation 
49. NSIC provides training through Incubation Centres for the purpose of 
skill development and employment generation. The NSIC also offers the 
demand driven -industries oriented training programm es which caters to 
high-tech areas as well as conventional trades. The Committee recommends 
that NSIC should explore the possibility of establishing more Incubation 
Centres in order to impart training to the potential entrepreneurs/youth in 
the areas of bu siness operation for their gainful employment. If need be, 
additional funds may be sought at the RE stage to continue imparting more 
training to the potential entrepreneurs/youth/artisans with special focus on 
women artisans for the overall growth of the MSME Sector. 
 
(Para 83) 

 51 
Action Taken Replies 
  As unavailability of Built -up space and recurring expenditure are 
constraint for setting up Livelihood Business Incubation Centre (LBIS), 
NSIC will continue to explore possibility of setting up LBI at other locations 
by sending communications to State Government s, PSUs and institutions to 
provide built up space to house the LBIs. Further, more fund will be 
demanded under various schemes for imparting more training to the 
potential entrepreneurs/youth. 
Recommendation/Observation 
50. The Committee notes that the BE for the FY 2022 -23 was Rs. 20.00 
crore which was reduced to Rs. 4.00 crore only at the RE stage and the 
Actual Expenditure (up to 31.01.2023) is zero. However, an amount of Rs. 
22.23 crore has been projected as BE for the FY 2023 -24. Considering such 
an important and crucial Scheme like the ASPIRE for innovative 
entrepreneurship and generating employment opportunities in agro -rural 
sector by skilling, up -skilling and re -skilling unemployed and existing se lf-
employed/wage earners in new technology, the Committee recommends that 
more budgetary provisions should be made for the scheme at the RE stage 
and the Ministry of Finance should be approached in this regard. 
(Para 108) 
Action Taken Replies 
The authoriza tion for disbursal of Rs.4.00 crore was issued by the 
Ministry of MSME to the Central Nodal Agency (CNA) on 03.03.2023 for 
further release to the Host Institutions of the LBIs. The projected amount of 
Rs.22.23 crore has been proposed predominantly on accou nt of meeting the 
target of 22 LBIs to be approved during the FY 2023 -24 besides meeting the 
demand for release of 2nd & 3rd installment to the already approved LBIs 
and the Operational expenditure support to the existing LBIs as per the 
extant scheme guidelines. The additional fund requirements at the RE stage 
will be evaluated in view of the approved LBIs under the scheme and the 
status of expenditure under the revised fund flow mechanism of the Deptt. of 
Expenditure, Ministry of Finance. 
Recommendation/Observation 
51. It is learnt that performance of the MSMEs during the last five years 
has not been very encouraging. The Committee recommends that a 
comprehensive study needs to be conducted by the Ministry of MSME to 
fathom the current situation of MSME se ctor in the country and to find out 

 52 
the exact impact of COVID -19 Pandemic on the MSME sector and to know 
whether the MSME sector has actually recovered from the pandemic effect 
or still reeling under the impacts of the Covid Pandemic. The Committee 
may als o like to be apprised about the findings of the study for its 
consideration considering the fact that a resilient and dynamic MSME 
Sector will be instrumental in realizing the goal of Make in India and Atma 
Nirbhar Bharat (Self Reliant India). 
(Para 140) 
Action Taken Replies 
As recommended by Committee, t he Ministry of MSME will 
undertake a comprehensive study on the current situation of MSME sector in 
the country and to find out the exact impact of COVID -19 Pandemic on the 
MSME sector. A study was also conducted by SIDBI from September, 2021 
to January, 2022, comprising 1,029 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSMEs) spread across 20 States and 2 UTs revealed that 67% of the 
respondent MSMEs were temporarily closed up to a period of three months 
due to COVID-19 Pandemic

CHAPTER – I 
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY 
Recommendation/Observation 
1. The Committee notes that the Budgetary allocation o f Rs 6171.63 crore for 
the Financial Year 2023-24 is the highest ever enha ncement in comparison to the 
BE of the previous years. The Committee notes the s ignificant enhanced fund 
allocation to the Ministry and hopes that the alloc ation would be utilized 
effectively in achieving the targets set by the Min istry for the Financial Year 2023-
24. 
 (Para 7) 
Action Taken Replies 
Against the Budget projection of Rs.6574.93 crore, Ministry of Heavy Industries 
has been allocated a fund of Rs.6171.63 crore which  is almost double the previous 
year’s budget. The major allocations of funds are f or FAME India Scheme-II 
(Rs.5171.97 crore), Production linked Incentive (PL I) Scheme for Automobiles 
and Auto Components (Rs.604.00 crore) and Enhanceme nt of Competitiveness in 
the India Capital Goods Sector (Rs.250.00 crore) for the Financial Year 2023-24. It 
is hoped to utilize the full allocation during 2023-24. 
 
(i).  AUTO: The FAME India Scheme Phase II is demand driven.  T his scheme 
helps in demand generation of electric vehicles by way of reducing the cost of 
acquisition of such vehicles. As the demand of elec tric vehicles increases, the pace 
in implementation of FAME India Scheme increases an d the fund utilization also 
increases.  
  The sale of electric vehicles under this scheme h as significantly increased 
over the years as seen from the table below:

 FY 2021-22 FY 2022-23

As a result, the electric vehicle incentive disburs ement is expected to increase to 
meet the increasing demand of electric vehicles. 
(ii) . PLI Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components: Under this scheme, FY 
2023-24 is the first disbursement year as per the n otification issued by the MHI. 
Therefore, Rs. 604.00 crores has been allocated for  meeting the expenditure as per 
the scheme incentive outlay. 
(iii). Capital Goods Sector: It is pertinent to mention that under the Capital Goods 
Scheme Phase II, a  total of 27 projects with Proje ct Cost of Rs.909.38 crores have 
already been sanctioned so far. Thus, the total com mitment of MHI contribution 
for these projects is Rs.725.46 crore i.e. approx 8 0% of the project cost. MHI was 
able to utilize Rs.199.25 crores allocated for FY 2022-23. The budgetary allocation 
under the Scheme for FY 2023-24 is Rs 250 crores. T herefore, MHI expects to 
fully utilize the amount allotted under BE 2023-24 for the projects sanctioned so 
far and also for the projects which will be sanctioned in the current Financial Year.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
2. The Committee observes that for the Financial Year 2023-24, the Budget 
Projection of the Ministry was Rs 6574.93 crore against which Ministry of Finance 
has allocated Rs 6171.63 crore, which is about 93.8 7% of the projection, as such, 
there is a shortfall of Rs 403.30 crore in allocati on. The budgetary allocation for 
the major Schemes of Ministry such as FAME India an d Scheme for 
Competitiveness in Capital Goods Sector have also s hortfall in allocation for the 
FY2023-24. The Committee recommends that the Minist ry should take all-out 
effort to strategize and utilize the major part of the allocations timely and if need 
be, allocation for more funds should be projected a t the RE stage to avoid any 
hindrance  in the effective implementation of these Flagship Schemes. 
 (Para 12) 
Action Taken Replies 
The recommendation of the Committee is noted. Under  the Scheme for 
Competitiveness in Capital Goods Sector, MHI is exp editing process of 
sanctioning of proposals and has already sanctioned  Rs 909 crores worth of 
proposals till 22.05.2023 out of total outlay of th e scheme of Rs.1207 crores. 
Further sufficient proposals for development of nic he technologies from different 
Institutes spread across India are under examinatio n for approval. As mentioned 

4 
 
earlier, MHI was able to utilize funds to the tune of Rs 199.25 crores, allocated at 
RE stage for FY 2022-23. MHI will make best efforts  to ensure that Rs 250 crores 
allotted for year 2023-24 are also fully utilized. The allocation shall be reviewed at 
RE stage based on fund utilization and demand recei ved from the Project 
Implementation Organizations (PIOs) and more funds will be sought at RE stage, if 
required.  
Recommendation/Observation 
3. The Committee notes that there were various unforeseen circumstances such 
as Covid-19 Pandemic induced constraints, etc. due to which the major portions of 
the funds were surrendered in the FYs 2019-20, 2020 -21 and 2021-22. It was also 
observed that under the major and important Scheme for Enhancement of 
Competitiveness in Capital Goods Sector, surrender of huge amounts were made 
continuously since FYs 2019-20 to 2021-22 due to re ceipt of less number of 
proposals from the implementing agencies. The Commi ttee is of the view that huge 
surrender of funds defeats the very objective of th e schemes envisioned. The 
Committee desires that the Ministry should analyze and find out the reasons why 
adequate number of proposals were not received unde r the scheme and should 
devise a plan to promote the Schemes through awaren ess programmes/campaigns 
so that the funds made available to the Schemes are  properly utilized and the goal 
of Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat Mission is realized for the overall 
economic development of the country. 
(Para 17) 
Action Taken Replies  
MHI takes note of the above observation of the Comm ittee. It is submitted that   in 
order to further boost the Capital Goods Sector, on  January 25, 2022, the Ministry 
of Heavy Industries (MHI) has notified the Scheme o n Enhancement of 
Competitiveness in The Indian Capital Goods Sector-  Phase-II for providing 
assistance for Technology Development and creation of common Services 
Infrastructure. The scheme has a financial outlay of Rs. 1207 crores with budgetary 
support of Rs.975 crore and Industry Contribution o f Rs.232 crores. Since 
the  notification of the Scheme, several project pr oposals have been received and 
after due diligence, as per the guidelines of the S cheme, a total of 27 projects with 
Project cost of Rs. 909.38 crores have been sanctio ned so far.  The total 
commitment of MHI contribution for these projects i s Rs.725.46 crore i.e. approx 
80% of the project cost.  MHI was able to gainfully make a utilization of Rs.199.25 

5 
 
crores out of the allocated amount of Rs.199.32 crores at RE stage for FY 2022-23. 
Thus, MHI was able to fully utilize the allocated funds for the FY 2022-23.  
   Further, a large number of promotional events fo r the promotion of Capital 
Goods Sector and Capital Goods Scheme have been sup ported in the FY 2022-23. 
These events have been organised by several Industr y Associations and 
organizations such as Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC), Textile 
Machinery Manufacturers Association (TMMA), ICEMA, IIT BHU, Mahratta 
Chambers of Commerce, Industry and Agriculture (MCC IA), VNIT Nagpur etc. 
Further, on its own, MHI has also organized followi ng two major events to create 
awareness/ importance of Capital Goods Sector towards ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’: 
i. A one day Conference on Industry 4.0 with theme “In dustry 4.0 -Challenges 
Ahead" was organised on 7th October 2022 at Kevadia , Gujarat. The event 
was chaired by Dr. Mahendra Nath Pandey, Hon'ble Mi nister for Heavy 
Industries and was also attended by Shri Bhupendra Patel, Hon’ble Chief 
Minister, Gujarat and Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar, Hon’ ble MoS for Heavy 
Industries. The deliberations in the Conference has  emphasized upon faster 
adoption of Industry 4.0 on a larger scale and maki ng India a manufacturing 
powerhouse. More than 200 participants from various  industries, Academic 
institutions, research institutes, skill councils e tc. from various parts of the 
Country attended the event and more than 15,000 att ended the Conference 
through online mediums. The event was well apprecia ted by the participants 
as it also provided them an opportunity to interact  and share their

8. The Committee notes that the passenger car sector o f India grew 
significantly as India became the 3rd largest manufacturer of passenger cars in the 
world.  At the same time, in 2-Wheeler sector, Indi a has slipped to 2nd position 
from the 1st position as compared to the FY2021-22.  While the Committee 
commends the efforts of the Ministry in respect of manufacture of passenger cars, 
it however notes with concern the decline in manufa cturing of 2-Wheelers in view 
of the extensive use of 2-Wheelers in the country. The Committee is of the view that 
the Ministry should conduct a holistic study and lo ok into the shortcomings that 
have caused India to slip down to 2nd position in m anufacturing of 2-Wheelers so 
that corrective measures can be taken timely to enable India to regain its position.         
                       
(Para 20) 
Action Taken Replies 
As per the information received from SIAM, India ha d manufactured more than 25 
million units of two-wheelers in the year 2018, whi ch has been the highest ever. 
Thereafter, for the next two-years India had posted  decline in manufacturing of 
Two-wheelers by (-) 12% and (-) 23% in 2019 and 202 0, respectively, compared to 
the preceding year. 
  Though the decline in manufacturing of two-wheele rs has been due to Covid 
in the year 2020, however, this industry witnessed a de-growth even in the pre-
Covid period, in the year 2019. In the year 2021, t here was a slight increase in the 
manufacturing of two-wheelers to 18.9 million units  and in 2022 to about 19.6 
million units. This increase was primarily driven b y the demand in the Exports 
market, while the domestic demand for two-wheelers in 2021 remained almost flat 
and there was a marginal increase in 2022. 
 There are multiple factors that have led to this de-growth:  

11 
 
• Regulatory Impact: Several new mandatory regulation s were introduced in 
India that led to the increase in cost of the Two-W heelers. In the year 2018, 
Government of India mandated Anti-Lock Braking Syst ems (ABS) for all Two-
Wheelers above 125 cc and Combined Braking Systems (CBS) for all Two-
Wheelers up to 125 cc. Subsequently in 2020, within  a period of 3 years, it was 
mandated for all Two-Wheelers to move directly to B S VI Emission norms, from 
BS IV emission levels which were only introduced across the country in year 2017. 
Recently, from 1 st  April 2023, the Two-Wheeler industry has been agai n mandated 
to move to next stage of BS VI Emission norms, which has additional requirements 
on On-Board Diagnostics (OBD) systems and these req uirements would be again 
made more stringent from April 2025, resulting in i ncrease in the cost of the Two-
Wheelers.  
• Mandatory Long Term 3 rd  Party Insurance: In the year 2018, Hon’ble 
Supreme Court of India mandated payment of 5-year u pfront premium for 3 rd  party 
insurance based on the recommendation of the Suprem e Court Committee on Road 
Safety. The premium was also increased in the year 2022, which has put further 
burden on the two-wheeler consumers.  
• Increase in Commodity Prices: Following the Covid P andemic in 2020, 
prices of commodities and shortages of electronic items, especially in 2021, pushed 
up the input cost of the two-wheelers significantly.  
• Recovery of the Rural Economy: A large portion of t he Two-Wheeler sales 
in India is driven through rural market, especially  for the motorcycles. Following 
the Covid, the rural segment has recovered at a muc h slower pace compared to the 
urban areas in India, which has resulted in subdued  growth of the two-wheeler 
segment, compared to much faster growth in Passenge r Vehicles or Commercial 
vehicles.  
• Higher Lending Rates: Recently RBI has hiked the le nding rates. These have 
impacts on the rates offered by NBFCs to the consum ers. NBFCs support about 
60% of two-wheeler sales in the country. Hence, non-availability of credits at lower 
rates has also impacted the Two-Wheeler purchases. 
 
Recommendation/Observation

Action Taken Replies 
India is already largest manufacturer of tractors i n the world. The production of

The organized farm machinery sector includes about 250 medium to large -scale 
units that produce sophisticated machinery. 
In order to lay special emphasis towards promotion of agricultural mechanization 
in the country and to bring more inclusiveness, Sub -Mission on Agricultural 
Mechanization (SMAM) is being implemented by DA&FW since April 2014 with 
the major objectives of increasing the reach of far m mechanization to small and 
marginal farmers and to the regions where availabil ity of farm power is low; 
promoting ‘Custom Hiring Centres’ to offset the adv erse economies of scale 
arising due to small landholding and high cost of i ndividual ownership of 
machines; and creating awareness among stakeholders  through demonstration and 
capacity building activities. 
Under SMAM, financial assistance for purchase of ag ricultural machines and 
equipments by the farmers on individual ownership b asis is provided to the small 
and marginal farmers, Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tri be farmers, Women farmers 
and North Eastern Region Farmers @50% of the cost o f machine with applicable 
ceiling limits. For other farmers the rate of finan cial assistance is @40% of the 
cost. 
Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) and Hi-Tech, High Productive Equipment Hubs for 
Custom Hiring aims at creating infrastructure for m aking available machines and 
equipments to the farmers on rental basis. Financia l assistance @ 40% of the 
project cost is provided to Rural Entrepreneurs (Ru ral youth and farmer as an 
entrepreneur), Cooperative Societies of farmers, Fa rmer Producer Organizations 
(FPOs), SHGs and Panchayats. The project cost of CH Cs can be up to Rs. 60 lakh 
and that of Hi-tech hubs can be up to Rs. 250 lakh. 

13 
 
Financial assistance @ 80% of the project cost is p rovided to Cooperative 
Societies, FPOs, SHGs and Panchayats to set up Farm  Machinery Banks of project 
cost up to Rs. 10 lakhs in identified villages in l ow mechanized States. For the 
North-Eastern States, the rate of financial assista nce is @95% of the project cost 
for the projects up to Rs. 10 Lakhs.  
Since inception of the scheme, Rs.6120.85 Crore hav e been provided to various 
States for distribution of 15,23,650 numbers of agricultural machineries. The States 
have also established 43,954 numbers of Custom Hiri ng Centres/Hi-tech hubs of 
high-cost machinery/Village level farm machinery ba nks to ensure easy 
availability of agricultural machines and equipments to the farmers on rental basis. 
The Department has also implemented a Central Secto r Scheme on Crop Residue 
Management in the States of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and NCT of Delhi. 
Under this schemes, during the period from 2018-19 to 2022-23, more than 2.41 
lakh various agricultural machines and equipments s uitable for in-situ and ex-situ 
management of crop residue have been provided to th e farmers on individual 
ownership basis with financial assistance @ 50% of the cost of machines and to 
more than 38000 Custom Hiring Centres with financia l assistance @ 80% of the 
project cost. 
The interventions under the above stated schemes ha s helped in increasing the 
level farm power availability for various farming o perations in the country and 
thus contributed to increasing the production and p roductivity of farms for higher 
income of the farmers. It has also helped boosting the agricultural machinery 
manufacturing sector of the country.

and charge levels of the battery and alert the driv er if any anomalies

REPORT 
 
Electric vehicles are gaining popularity across the globe. Due to fast 
depletion of fossil fuels, the automotive industry is also shifting from 
traditional fuel based technology to eco-friendly technologies. The 
automotive sector has emerged as one of the most dynamic and rapidly 
growing sector in the world. The sector has witnessed remarkable progress 
and is now considered a key contributor to economic growth of the nations. 
The growth of this sector in India has been fuelled by several factors, 
including rising income levels, increasing urbanization, improved road 
infrastructure, and the expansion of the middle-class population. The sector 
encompasses a wide range of vehicles, catering to various segments and 
consumer preferences. Two-wheelers, such as motorcycles and scooters, and 
Three Wheelers dominate the automotive market of developing nations such 
as India, owing to their affordability and convenience in navigating 
congested urban areas. Passenger cars have also witnessed significant 
growth, with a rising demand for compact and mid-size vehicles. 
Furthermore, the commercial vehicle segment, including trucks and buses, 
plays a pivotal role in supporting robust transportation and logistics network. 
 
2. The automotive sector also faces its share of challenges. These include 
the need for continuous technological advancements, stringent emission 
norms, infrastructure development, and skilled labour availability etc. 
Nonetheless, industry stakeholders, including manufacturers, policymakers, 
and consumers are actively working towards overcoming these obstacles and 
fostering a sustainable and competitive automotive ecosystem. Pollution is a 
significant concern in the automotive sector, primarily due to the rapid 
growth of vehicles on the roads and the associated emissions. However, 
efforts are made within the auto sector to mitigate its environmental impact 
and promote sustainability.  
Indian Automotive Sector: 
3. The Automotive Industry in India has come a long way from its 
nascent state at the time of India’s independence in 1947 to its present day 
dynamic form. Today, the industry produces a wide range of automobiles 
and auto-components catering to both the domestic as well as foreign 
markets. The development of the industry has been shaped by the demand on 
the one hand and the government interventions on the other. 
 
4. India represents the third largest automobile market of Passenger 
vehicles and Commercial vehicles in the world. India is the world's largest 
manufacturer of Three Wheelers, second largest manufacturer of Two-

2 
 
Wheelers, and fourth largest manufacturer of Passenger Vehicles. Indian 
Automotive Industry has the presence of all Global automobile
